notes: The Commons' people (Harbor Ward's building on the Ark, design/act-3.md). With the Commons standing, the survivors you woke live there, each with a light of their own, and say something of their own: one of their district's lines, the same one each time (by who they are). And the Wardfolk who came over from the Ward when it was built, who never wore a Lanyard: what they say depends on whether Noor came home. People talking: plain type. Placeholder writing.

kestrel: Nobody tells the beans when to come up. I'd forgotten that.
I keep a bed of greens by the Commons door. It grows what it likes.
loop: Four of us sat in that carriage for days. Now we argue about whose turn it is to cook.
I still listen for the trains. There aren't any. I don't mind.
We rode the same line for years and never spoke. We know each other's names now.
tideworks: Nobody's told me what shift it is in weeks. I keep one anyway. Habit.
They asked me to run the kitchen rota. I said I'd never run anything. They said, start.
mercy: I still wake at the hour it used to wake me. Then I remember I can lie there.
There's a woman here who sets bones. Nobody assigned her. She just does.
I sat with the night nurse till morning. We talked. That's all. It helped.
greywater: We turn the pumps by hand now. It's slower. We know why it's done.
Forty of us kept them going for nine days. I'd do it again. I'd rather not.
vellum: I read the old papers now. The real ones. It's hard going.
Somebody pinned the Council Order to the Commons wall. People stop and read it twice.

noor_home: Noor's up that mast half the night. Says it hears what the Lattice never bothered with.
We never had the Lanyard. We had each other's doors. It's the same here, near enough.
noor_stayed: Noor stayed back in the Ward. Somebody has to keep the lanterns lit.
We never had the Lanyard. We had each other's doors. It's the same here, near enough.
